newsitem.title: UK: UK November budget has not helped business - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK November budget has not helped business - survey.

text.p: Most British companies believe last month's budget will leave them no better off, a report claimed on Monday.

The survey by the Institute of Management reported that 71 percent of managers said they had not personally gained from the budget in financial terms and almost a quarter (23 percent) believe they would be worse off.
Only four percent expect to be spending more as a result of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's measures.
Highlighting widespread scepticism among managers about the government's forecasts for the UK economy in 1997, the report said they were also dissatisfied with the budget's implications for business.

The Institute of Management report said some 53 percent of managers believe the budget focuses on short-term political issues rather than long-term economic matters, while almost half do not believe the budget is good for business.
Given the UK's economic performance, 59 percent of managers believe the cuts in income tax were not justified.
Among measures targeted at small businesses employing up to 100 people, only proposals on the uniform business rate found favour with those managers, the report said.
Roger Young, director general of the Institute of Management said: "Managers do not share the Chancellor's breezy confidence about the UK economy.
"A shiver runs up their spines as they face the chilling prospect of rising interest rates and inflation.
"In the cold light of day, they believe the risks taken could blow away any rewards generated by the budget."
